profile.reading:
This entry covers two adjoining CyrusOne buildings, SAT10 and SAT11, on the far west side of Bexar County near San Antonio's Texas Research Park data center cluster. Trade press reporting from Data Center Dynamics, citing a Texas Department of Licensing and Regulation project filing, places SAT10 and SAT11 at 15355 Lambda Drive, San Antonio, Texas 78245, on a site described as more than 25 acres, with that same November 2023 reporting stating plainly that further details on those two projects had not been shared publicly at that time. This research session found no operator webpage, later press account, or public filing that discloses square footage, IT capacity, utility feed size, or standby generation for SAT10 or SAT11 specifically, and no source naming an opening date or construction status more recent than that 2023 filing report. Those are treated here as documented gaps rather than assumed to be small or inactive. Because the Lambda Drive address comes from press description of a licensing filing rather than from a source this session could independently geocode and check against this row's stored coordinates, it is recorded here as reported, not added to or substituted for this row's own address.

SAT10 and SAT11 sit within a much larger, well documented CyrusOne buildout in this same corridor. CyrusOne's first San Antonio data center opened in 2012, and by CyrusOne's own account at a July 2024 groundbreaking attended by Bexar County Judge Peter Sakai and CPS Energy officials, cumulative CyrusOne capital investment in San Antonio had reached roughly 1 billion dollars. That groundbreaking, for a campus CyrusOne called its fifth in San Antonio, corresponds by square footage to a separate two story, four data hall, 279,730 square foot filing that press and licensing records identify as SAT8 and SAT9, sited near CyrusOne's existing SAT5 facility on Omicron Drive, distinct from the Lambda Drive project. Other named CyrusOne buildings in the same San Antonio cluster include SAT1, a 9 megawatt facility on Westover Hills Boulevard, SAT2, a 36 megawatt facility on the same street, and SAT5, an 18 megawatt facility on Omicron Drive, figures reported in trade press rather than confirmed here as current operator disclosures for those specific buildings.

The wider Bexar County record shows both real strain and real growth. San Antonio Report, a nonprofit local news outlet, reported in early 2026 that CPS Energy supplies electricity to 21 data centers citywide, generating about 110 million dollars in annual revenue from that customer class, with 59 additional data center projects in various stages of planning, and separately that Bexar County is home to at least 30 data centers, with CyrusOne and Vantage Data Centers together registering more than 1 billion dollars in Texas licensing tracked construction along the roughly two mile stretch of Omicron Drive since 2020. CPS Energy has published a large load interconnection process guide for customers seeking new capacity, and ERCOT commissioned an independent technical review of CPS Energy's large load additions project in 2025, evidence that grid capacity planning for this whole cluster, which includes the Lambda Drive site, is an active and documented utility concern. No Bexar County Commissioners Court tax abatement agreement, City of San Antonio Chapter 380 grant, or contested public hearing naming SAT10 or SAT11 specifically was found in this research session.

reading.body:
CyrusOne SAT10 and SAT11 are two adjoining buildings on more than 25 acres near San Antonio's Texas Research Park, filed with the state in November 2023 but carrying no published specifications for IT capacity, power draw, or opening date. The operator has disclosed neither square footage, utility connection size, nor standby generation for these two facilities specifically, and trade press reported in 2023 that such details had not been shared publicly at that time. This is a documented gap rather than evidence the buildings are small or inactive.

These two facilities sit within a much larger CyrusOne buildout in the same San Antonio corridor that began in 2012 and had accumulated roughly 1 billion dollars in capital investment by mid-2024. Named sister facilities nearby include SAT1 at 9 megawatts, SAT2 at 36 megawatts, and SAT5 at 18 megawatts, with a separate 279,730 square foot, four data hall project filed for construction in 2024 and 2025. The Lambda Drive site where SAT10 and SAT11 sit is part of the same cluster now undergoing active grid capacity planning by CPS Energy and ERCOT, rather than a frontier or isolated outpost.

Bexar County hosts at least 30 data centers, with CPS Energy serving 21 citywide and 59 more in planning stages. CyrusOne and Vantage Data Centers together account for more than 1 billion dollars in licensed construction along the Omicron Drive corridor since 2020, and the data center customer class generates roughly 110 million dollars in annual revenue for the utility. Because SAT10 and SAT11 carry no published capacity figures, they do not rank among the 19 facilities in Texas with disclosed megawatt counts, though their parent operator is a major incumbent in the state's most constrained grid district.
